stories.title: Signature Global bags 4-Star GRESB Rating - Construction Week India
Signatureglobal reports GRESB score of 97.8
stories.summary: Signatureglobal attained a GRESB score of 97.8 out of 100, up from 84 last year. The company secured a 4-star rating and ranks 12th globally among its residential peers. It achieved a perfect score in the reporting category. Sustainability excellence is now a measurable pursuit.

stories.title: Signature Global GRESB score rises to 97.8
stories.summary: Signature Global recorded a GRESB score of 97.8, an increase from its debut score of 84. The company earned a 4-star rating and ranks 12th globally among residential peers. It also reported planting over 9,700 trees during the fiscal year. Ratings have a way of climbing.

stories.title: Signatureglobal reports GRESB score surge
stories.summary: Signatureglobal announced a GRESB score of 97.8 out of 100, rising from an initial 84. The firm earned a 4-star rating and ranks 12th globally among residential and listed peers. It achieved a 100 percent score in the reporting category. Disclosure is now a competitive sport.

stories.title: India mandates CSR spending for qualifying companies
stories.summary: Under Section 135 of the Companies Act, qualifying companies in India must commit at least 2 percent of their average net profit from the three preceding years to eligible activities. Corporate social responsibility is a statutory duty rather than a goodwill gesture. The law does not offer opt-outs.

stories.title: Greater Amman Municipality issues first sustainability report
stories.summary: The Greater Amman Municipality has published its first corporate sustainability report to document environmental, social and governance performance. The report follows Global Reporting Initiative standards to improve institutional transparency. The municipality intends to use the document to establish a framework for monitoring its future performance.

stories.title: Greaves Cotton files sustainability report for FY 2025-26
stories.summary: Greaves Cotton Limited filed its business responsibility and sustainability report for fiscal year 2025-26. The company reported avoiding over 3.1 million kilograms of CO2 equivalent emissions and targets a 13 percent reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030. Independent assurance was provided by Agile ESG Advisors.

stories.title: Parma Calcio releases first sustainability report
stories.summary: Parma Calcio has released the first sustainability report in the club's history. The document outlines strategies across environmental, social and governance spheres, citing the importance of wellbeing for future generations. The results were presented at the headquarters of Davines in the presence of government officials.

stories.title: Parma Calcio details environmental management model
stories.summary: Parma Calcio presented its environmental work through a management model called PlayGreen. The club converted Stadio Tardini lighting to LED technology in 2025 and now sources all electricity for its facilities from renewable origins. The club has officially certified its environmental management system to international standards.

stories.title: EU and UK to link carbon markets by 2028
stories.summary: The European Commission and the UK government have agreed to link their respective emissions trading systems starting in 2028. The deal aims to eliminate trade barriers for goods subject to carbon pricing and create a more liquid market. Allowances will be interchangeable for compliance purposes across both systems.

stories.title: Farmers receive first soil organic carbon credit payments
stories.summary: Farmers in Punjab and Haryana have received payments for soil organic carbon credits after adopting direct seeding and reduced tillage practices. Payments ranged from 3,000 to 15,000 rupees. The project aims to reduce water and labor usage while creating a new crop out of carbon sequestration.

stories.title: GeoDipa seeks partners for Patuha Unit-2 carbon credits
stories.summary: Indonesia's state-owned Geo Dipa Energi is seeking partners to commercialize carbon credits from its 55-megawatt Patuha Unit-2 geothermal project. Estimates suggest the project could generate significant emissions reductions. The company is currently exploring sales opportunities for the anticipated credits at the COP31 climate conference.

stories.title: Norway and Iceland to join CBAM in 2027
stories.summary: Businesses importing steel, aluminum, fertilizer, cement, electricity or hydrogen into the Nordic region face new compliance obligations starting 1 January 2027. Norway and Iceland are joining the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism. The 50-tonne threshold applies to all entities within the scope of the regulation.

stories.title: EU and UK ETS link may offer CBAM exemptions
stories.summary: The EU and UK have committed to linking their emissions trading systems by 2028. This agreement could determine whether UK goods face the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism. The exemption depends on the formal ratification of the deal and the integration of the two carbon markets.

stories.title: Ghana earns forest carbon credits
stories.summary: Ghana has become the first African country to receive carbon credits under the ART-TREES standard. The government was issued 6.57 million credits for verified forest protection, with sales expected to raise 43 million dollars. The achievement was announced at the COP31 climate conference in Turkey.

stories.title: EU and UK finalize carbon market linkage deal
stories.summary: The EU and UK have concluded negotiations to link their emissions trading systems by 2028. The deal is expected to support the carbon capture and storage industry, with projections suggesting billions in potential investment by 2040. Integrated markets are intended to lower costs for industrial emitters.

stories.title: UP and IIT Roorkee launch carbon credit pilot
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh and IIT Roorkee have launched a pilot project in Saharanpur to convert soil and tree carbon into verified credits. The model aims to provide farmers with additional income through climate-friendly agricultural practices. The initiative seeks to link carbon sequestration directly to market-based financial incentives.

stories.title: COP31 collapse casts shadow over shipping’s net-zero showdown
stories.summary: Global climate negotiations in Turkey concluded without a final agreement after nearly 200 countries failed to reach consensus on fossil fuels and climate finance. The collapse occurred as shipping industry decarbonisation talks resume at the International Maritime Organization in London. The summit ended after record overtime.

stories.title: Market watch: COP31 talks collapse with no deal reached
stories.summary: The UN COP31 climate conference in Turkey ended without a deal after nations clashed over fossil fuel references and financial commitments. The summit, which ran for a record duration, failed to secure an agreement from the EU, Pacific island nations, and other participating countries.

stories.title: Cop31: Why the UN climate summit ended in failure
stories.summary: The annual UN climate summit concluded without a final agreement, marking the first such failure in over 20 years. While the conference agenda was adopted quickly on day one, negotiations stalled in the second week over the draft text and global temperature targets.

stories.title: COP31 ends in failure as nations clash over fossil fuels
stories.summary: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey concluded without a final agreement after nearly 200 nations failed to reach consensus. The talks extended more than 49 hours beyond the scheduled closing time, making it the longest UN climate conference on record. Climate advocates expressed disappointment.

stories.title: Why did the UK reject the COP31 deal? Britain's stance on the Antalya climate outcome - Nacionale
Cop31 failure sends message to people impacted by climate change
stories.summary: The COP31 summit concluded without a final agreement after failing to explicitly link climate change to fossil fuels. The draft text focused on multi-hazard early warning systems rather than addressing the primary causes of the crisis. The previous agreement to transition away from fossil fuels remains unhonoured.

stories.title: COP31 ends in deadlock, leaving Ethiopia to pick up the pieces
stories.summary: The UN climate summit in Turkey ended without a final cover decision following a record 44 hours of overtime. Nations failed to agree on language regarding fossil fuels, energy policy, and climate finance. Ethiopia is scheduled to host the next summit in Addis Ababa.

stories.title: Profound frustration as COP31 talks collapse in Turkey
stories.summary: COP31 talks collapsed after European and climate-vulnerable nations rejected a draft agreement that excluded references to fossil fuels. Saudi Arabia, Russia, and other petro-states blocked the inclusion of the leading cause of the climate crisis. This is the third time UN climate talks have failed.

stories.title: A dead end in Antalya
stories.summary: The COP31 summit in Turkey ended without a final political declaration after joint presidents halted negotiations following a two-day extension. The European Union rejected the draft text as unacceptable. It is the first climate summit since 2009 to conclude without a cover text.

stories.title: Why automated product carbon footprints aren’t yet decision-grade
stories.summary: New tools have reduced the time required to calculate product carbon footprints from months to minutes. Despite the increased availability of automated data, suppliers report that buyers frequently request footprint information but do not incorporate the findings into their actual purchasing decisions.

stories.title: The circular economy depends on waste-pickers
stories.summary: Thousands of waste-pickers in cities like Bogota collect recyclable materials that would otherwise end up in landfills. Despite being described as the human infrastructure of the circular economy, their labour remains largely underestimated in public policies and narratives regarding the ecological transition.

stories.title: IKEA leads brands driving the circular economy
stories.summary: According to the Circularity Gap Report 2026, only 7.2 percent of materials entering the global economy are cycled back into use. Closing this gap requires industrial-scale redesigns of how products are engineered and repaired. Sustainability Magazine recently ranked top brands based on their structural influence across value chains.

stories.title: City in Portugal discusses solutions for a circular economy
stories.summary: The Porsche Coimbra Service Centre and the University of Coimbra are hosting an event on 23 May to promote sustainable solutions in the automotive sector. The meeting aims to publicise innovations in circularity and raise awareness regarding recycling processes within the industry.

stories.title: Indonesia and Netherlands team up to reform waste management
stories.summary: The Indonesian Ministry of Environment and the Dutch government signed a memorandum of understanding on waste management and circular economy cooperation for 2026 to 2030. The agreement was finalised during the COP31 summit to support efforts in reducing plastic pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.

stories.title: Taiwan to cooperate in joint circular economy
stories.summary: Taiwan will partner with international entities on circular economy initiatives following the COP31 summit. Minister of Environment Peng Chi-ming stated that the nation must improve resource efficiency, as it relies on imports for 76.14 percent of its raw materials to support its high-tech manufacturing sectors.

stories.title: Indonesia and Netherlands strengthen waste management cooperation
stories.summary: The Indonesian Ministry of Environment and the Dutch government signed a bilateral agreement on waste management and the circular economy for the 2026 to 2030 period. The collaboration, announced at COP31, aims to accelerate the transition to circularity and reduce national greenhouse gas emissions.

stories.title: Circular economy generates up to USD 15.8 billion in Brazil
stories.summary: A survey by the National Confederation of Industry indicates the circular economy generates up to 15.8 billion USD in Brazil. Presented at COP31, the study found that funds allocated to circularity account for 3.5 to 10.3 percent of the country's sustainable finance market.

stories.title: Namibian schoolchildren turn waste into resources
stories.summary: Students at St. Barnabas Primary School in Windhoek are repurposing discarded plastic bottles and bags to create models. The project highlights local efforts to teach children about the circular economy and resource management.

stories.title: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy secures orders worth INR 2,050 crore
stories.summary: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy has secured domestic orders and an L1 bid with a combined value exceeding INR 2,050 crore. The company received a turnkey contract for a 600 MWh Battery Energy Storage System project from a public sector undertaking in Gujarat. The projects are currently underway.

stories.title: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy secures orders worth INR 2,050 crore
Amazon plans $7 billion renewable energy investment in India by 2030
stories.summary: Amazon announced plans to invest $7 billion in Indian renewable energy projects by 2030. This adds to $4 billion already contracted. The company also unveiled four new wind and solar projects with a combined capacity of 934 MW, including its largest wind farm in Asia to date.

stories.title: ACME Solar wins 50 MW Gujarat renewable power bid
stories.summary: ACME Solar Holdings Ltd. secured a 50 MW renewable energy capacity bid at INR 4.58 per kWh. The project was awarded through Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Ltd.'s e-reverse auction for firm and dispatchable renewable power. The company continues to expand its participation in the Indian energy sector.

stories.title: Adani Energy Solutions wins 2,500 MW renewable power supply award
stories.summary: Adani Energy Solutions subsidiary Powerpulse Trading Solutions received a Letter of Award from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company for 1,750 MW of round-the-clock renewable power. A 750 MW greenshoe option could bring the total to 2,500 MW over 25 years. Supply begins in July 2028.

stories.summary: Adani Energy Solutions subsidiary Powerpulse Trading Solutions received a Letter of Award from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company for 1,750 MW of round-the-clock renewable power. A 750 MW greenshoe option could bring the total to 2,500 MW over 25 years. Supply begins in July 2028.

stories.summary: Adani Energy Solutions subsidiary Powerpulse Trading Solutions received a Letter of Award from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company for 1,750 MW of round-the-clock renewable power. stories.title: Chubu Electric invests INR 1,350 crore in Continuum Green Energy
stories.summary: Japan's Chubu Electric has invested INR 1,350 crore in Continuum Green Energy to support renewable power in India. The deal includes a board seat for a Chubu nominee and access to Japanese industrial clients. The companies have not disclosed the specific percentage of the stake acquired.

stories.title: Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal
stories.summary: Meta is rethinking its 2030 net-zero goal following a record increase in greenhouse gas emissions driven by AI data centers. The company claims its long-term ambitions remain unchanged, but its operating environment has shifted. The environment has apparently shifted quite a lot.

research.title: Beyond Resolution: Inference-Time Parameterized Temporal Consistency in Generative Regional Climate Downscaling
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: GCM-to-RCM downscaling emulation is dominated by generative diffusion models, but most existing work evaluates skill only per timestep, treating each field as an independent snapshot. This leaves open whether generated sequences are temporally coherent or merely. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Carbon dioxide responses shape estimates of Amazon forest vulnerability under solar geoengineering
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: The Amazon rainforest is vulnerable to warming and changes in rainfall, yet whether solar geoengineering can reduce conditions associated with forest loss remains uncertain. Stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) can offset greenhouse-gas-driven warming without fully restoring regional. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Japan-Europe spacecraft BepiColombo begins orbit of Mercury, with a glitch reported
research.summary: The mission will seek to answer questions about Mercury such as why it has a magnetic field, why ice exists in the polar craters of a sun-scorched planet, and what is the nature of enigmatic depressions called "hollows" on its surface

research.title: Maximum updraft velocity beyond CAPE: the role of boundary layer dynamics and pressure perturbations
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deep convective updraft velocities influence precipitation extremes, lightning, and the planetary energy budget. Convective Available Potential Energy (CAPE) is widely used to explain maximum updraft velocity ($w_{\max}$), but updrafts are also influenced by entrainment, boundary layer. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Natural analogs for geoengineering suggest modest radiative plant gains
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) to limit global warming overshoot would reduce total solar radiation while increasing the proportion of diffuse light reaching Earth's surface, creating competing effects on plant growth. Analog studies using volcanic eruptions show. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Stabilized negative viscosity governs ocean jets before, during and after they leave the coast
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Eddies in rotating turbulence can feed the jets that spawn them, resulting in the negative viscosity phenomenon. Taken alone, a negative viscosity represents up-gradient eddy fluxes and is often referred to as "antifriction" or "antidiffusion". Mathematically. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.summary: Such a frequency is uncommon but not unique this year, there were around 1.8 cyclones a year in the post-monsoon period in 1982-2022, with the average increasing after 2001. Three cyclones in three weeks: What’s happening in the Bay of Bengal? | Explained

research.title: Rosalind Franklin’s notes crack mystery of DNA’s most famous photo
research.summary: Photograph 51 is one of the most iconic images in the history of science, featuring in several lists of the most important photographs ever taken. Its fame comes not only from the role it played in revealing DNA’s helical structure but also from the controversy surrounding its use.
